prompt:
Use case: photorealistic-natural. Create ONE highly refined NORMAL RECTILINEAR architectural interior photo in landscape3:2, output2048x1360 or largest available. Input1: current apartment360 panorama is GEOMETRY/ADJACENCY evidence ONLY, NOT output projection. Keep the existing floor plan, original doors/windows and all previously approved functional layouts. DO NOT output360/equirectangular/fisheye, a collage, curved walls, a board of samples, an exterior or a close-up that loses the room. Correct straight verticals and a real28-32mm architectural lens, plausible small-apartment proportions. Every visible edge, reveal, textile seam and fixture must look built, not generic CGI: fine open wood grain at realistic scale, tiny eased edge, satin non-plastic metal, actual separate fabric weave, coherent tiled joints, properly supported shelves, meaningful surface contact shadows. Natural soft NEUTRAL daylight plus just a few local warm task pools; readable white balance, no overall yellow/orange haze, HDR halos or artificial blur. No people, text, visible brand logos, watermarks or cloned botanical art everywhere. This is an original home design informed by published general design principles, not a reproduction of a designer's named project.
STYLE: smoked natural oak, restrained dark cherry, warm-gray mineral plaster, muted moss/lichen linen, charcoal/aged bronze accents, neutral daylight
LEARNED DESIGN PRIORITIES: Keep the forest mood without all-over rustic orange timber or giant rope texture. Fine wool instead of chunky jute, tailored plain flax cushions instead of embossed floral fabric, slim downlight reading lamps instead of huge arch lamps, one small earth/ink abstract rather than generic botanical gallery. Straight-grain cherry/oak veneer, precise inset plinth and recessed pulls, thin eased timber edges, grouped window plants, subtle mineral variation.
EXACT LAYOUT: Original1.80m bed and entrance dressing zone, only original end exterior window, left side wall solid, wardrobes stay at entry, no added television, no fireplace, no bed facing invented window.
VISIBLE IMPROVEMENTS: Use an upholstered or timber-backed headboard with one readable material junction, small thin bedside ledge each side, individual downward reading light and discrete switch/charging, real duvet and linen seams, full-height closed wardrobe reveals and a reachable laundry pullout, mirror on actual solid panel, no bulky bench blocking foot route.
CAMERA: Eye1.30m normal rectilinear28-32mm photo from original bedroom entry towards bed showing one part of dressing cabinetry and original window, natural proportions.

stylingCorrection.prompt:
Use case: precise-object-edit. Edit ONLY the small objects and home-styling arrangement in this NORMAL3:2 architectural photograph. Keep camera, projection, original room scale, all built-ins, bed/desk/TV/sofa positions, windows, doors, materials, colour and light EXACTLY. User wants meaningful lived-in small decorations and coherent item placement, NOT random objects and NOT a bare showroom. Arrange a small number of functional personal items in thoughtful groupings, realistic hand-reach, coordinated muted natural palette, varied heights, credible contact shadows; no readable writing, people, logos or watermark. Do NOT add large furniture, new windows, arches, kitchen islands or extra floor clutter.
LIVED-IN STYLING: on one bedside ledge a small grouped tray holding reading book, tiny ceramic cup/water glass and charging phone placed neatly; another bedside gets only individual reading lamp and one small photo frame. Soft casually folded throw and two coordinated plain/stripe pillows, not a mountain of cushions. Wardrobe/dressing nook has contained jewelry/key dish, one small mirror and a linen laundry basket tucked at cabinet end, no random sculptures, perfume wall, plants around bed or clinical hotel staging.
These are modest daily objects; preserve at least half of working/table surfaces free. Do not turn this into an advertisement or cluttered decor shop. Keep source3:2 aspect and its native sharp detail.
